summary: Re-issue of TASK-UNBLOCK-01 after its round cap. The commit-hook exemption is deleted down to the one exact bookkeeping command, compared as the shell reads it; commit detection lives in tested Python and covers quoted option values, backticks, sh -c/bash -c/eval and any inline alias; a baselined file leaves the baseline once any commit touched it; rename sources stay in scope in every status; git path lists are NUL-separated; protected and frozen paths match regardless of case; a blocking review finding is dismissed only by a person, deferral also through a `finding` waiver, and `aegis next` hands that decision to a person. R-10, R-14 and R-25 amended, R-25 and R-26 added.

verification.note: 159 tests; bootstrap gate passes with two labelled, expiring budget waivers for oversized lens reports

deviations: Implemented by the session agent from the prepared bundle .aegis/changes/universal-01 steps 1-3, not by a dispatched aegis-builder; steps 4 (ADR-3) and 5 (B2) are left for their own tasks.
The whole uncommitted tree is still this task's scope (135 files): nothing has been committed since 00c7c9f, and committing is the repository owner's decision.
Spec edits to .aegis/specs/unblock-cycle/spec.md and ADR-2 are outside the lease by design (.aegis/ is never leased); they record R-14 and R-10 amendments and R-25, R-26.
Registered AEGIS_PATCH_ROOT (read by the bundle scripts under .aegis/changes/universal-01) and removed their machine-specific fallback path.

The task gate's trace check fails on aegis-sdd-framework-full.md: the owner's rename to docs/spec-v0.3-original.md was staged before adoption, and R-26 now lists rename sources. A deletion has no content to baseline. Committing it does not clear this task either: a commit that touches baselined paths puts them in scope for tasks based before it. The route is the owner committing the adoption state, then re-issuing this task on the new base (spec edge case, ARCHITECTURE §3, README limits, trace hint).

Three lens rounds ran (the cap): 25 findings, 19 resolved, 0 reopened, 6 advisory findings left open. The three records were clean at digest a950967e27166cb6; correcting the design lens's round-3 advisories about EVALUATION §8 moved the digest, so the records are stale and a fourth round is not allowed. EVALUATION §8 records this rather than calling the reviews green.

Found after the round budget was spent, so left for the re-issue: `aegis next` advises re-running a lens whose next round would exceed `policy.refinement_rounds`, instead of escalating. The docs-staleness warnings on ARCHITECTURE.md and README.md need `aegis docs attest --by <a person>`, which is the owner's signature, not an agent's.

The task gate is red on two checks, both outside what this change can fix: `trace` on aegis-sdd-framework-full.md (the owner's pre-adoption rename) and the three stale review records. Recorded here rather than as a failed verification command, because the task's own commands — make check, make lint — pass.

ABANDONED 2026-09-17, re-issued as TASK-UNBLOCK-03. Not because a finding was unresolved: all six blocking ones were fixed and the three lens records were clean. Two things arrived after the round budget was spent. First, the owner instructed the session to finish the work itself, which is the human decision the escalation waited for. Second, correcting the design lens's last advisories about EVALUATION §8 moved the digest, and a fourth round is not allowed. The successor carries R-1..R-26 unchanged plus the adoption-attribution rule (ADR-4, R-27) that makes the adoption commit possible at all, and the documentation defects a fresh review of the whole session found (R-28).
